## Claim + Dispatch — R34

`domain:devx` PM seat (#6023), session `session_01Pk26oZ12t5N1hwGW1m1MgC`. Branch: **`claude/issue-12353-docs-orphan-pages`**

### Epic territory check (⛔ this seat has made this mistake before, so it is done in writing)

Triage flagged the overlap: *"Note for the epic PM on #12243: … adopt into the subtree if in scope."*
I read `label:pm:epic` before dispatching. **#12243 has NOT adopted this card** — it is not in the
epic's sub-issue list. The epic's declared territory on this surface is:

> `content/docs/**` — frontmatter `title` / `description`, body headings

⇒ **Your face is body prose links and `meta.json` — ⛔ NOT frontmatter, ⛔ NOT headings.** Those belong
to the epic's still-open P1 lane (#12236–#12239), which rewrites frontmatter across ~403 files. Say in
the PR body which of the two faces you touched, so the boundary is auditable. ⛔ If the fix seems to
need a frontmatter or heading edit, **stop and report** — that is the epic PM's, not yours.

**Timeline fact you inherit, ⛔ don't re-derive it:** the epic's whole P0 lane is **closed**
(#12232 sitemap/robots, #12233, #12234, #12235) and so is P2 (#12240–#12242). That is why this card's
crawl found a working `/sitemap.xml` with 408 URLs on 2026-08-25 while the epic body of the same day
says there is none — #12232 landed in between. ⛔ No contradiction to chase.

### Zone 1 — TRIAGE RULING (⛔ 不可重裁,verbatim)

> Triage: graded and promoted to queue (`finding` → `pm:queue`); lands in `domain:devx` (docs-site
> surface: `content/docs/**` `meta.json` entries / section-index links, possibly a page deletion).
> … Charter: **per-page call as the body says** — for the two `kernel/contracts` pages, check first
> whether `content/docs/kernel/contracts/meta.json` is simply missing two entries (the body's own
> hypothesis); for `/docs/concepts/metadata-driven` and `/docs/protocol/backward-compatibility`,
> **decide link-in vs delete per page and record the reasoning**.

**⛔ Bounded by this seat: no page deletions in this PR.** Triage left deletion on the table and the
card calls it a per-page call, but deleting a published page is a user-visible retirement with a
different review shape than a link repair. If your per-page reasoning lands on *delete*, **write the
reasoning and stop there** — report it and I will file it as its own card. Link-in, `meta.json`, or a
reasoned "leave it" are the three outcomes this PR may carry.

### Zone 2 — PM 机制假设(⚠️ 须实测。⭐ Two of these I already half-broke for you — finish the job)

- **A2.1 — ⚠️ THE CARD'S OWN HYPOTHESIS IS ALREADY FALSE, ⛔ do not spend an hour on it.** The card and
  the charter both say to check whether `content/docs/kernel/contracts/meta.json` is "simply missing
  two entries". **It is not.** On `origin/main` it reads:
  ```json
  { "title": "Service Contracts",
    "pages": ["metadata-service", "auth-service", "storage-service", "data-engine", "cache-service"] }
  ```
  All five pages are listed, `auth-service` and `cache-service` included. ⇒ **The cause is elsewhere.**
  My reading, ⛔ unverified: `content/docs/kernel/contracts/index.mdx` carries only two outbound links
  (lines 159-160, to `/docs/plugins/development` and `/docs/kernel/services`) and links **none** of its
  five children, while the three non-orphans are linked from *other* pages entirely
  (`concepts/metadata-lifecycle.mdx`, `kernel/runtime-services/storage-service.mdx`,
  `protocol/objectql/index.mdx`). Measure it; if that is the shape, the section index is the fix site.
- **A2.2 — ⚠️ THE COUNT OF 4 MAY NO LONGER BE 4. Re-measure BEFORE you fix anything.** The measurement
  is six days old and this surface has had seven epic sub-issues land on it since. Concretely:
  `content/docs/getting-started/glossary.mdx:91` **does** carry a well-formed
  `[Metadata-Driven Development](/docs/concepts/metadata-driven)` on today's `origin/main`, which is an
  inbound link the card says does not exist. Either it was added since, or the glossary page is not in
  the sitemap, or the crawl misses that link shape. ⭐ **Whichever it is, it also tells you whether the
  card's instrument is still trustworthy for the other three** — that is the highest-value thing you
  can produce on this card, above any link you add.
- **A2.3 — I assume the fix is repo-side, not app-side.** If the orphaning turns out to come from
  `apps/docs` (nav generation, `meta.json` consumption), that is inside epic #12243's `apps/docs/**`
  territory ⇒ **stop and report**, ⛔ do not fix it here.
- **A2.4 — I assume "zero inbound links" means zero *rendered* links.** Reproduce with the card's own
  method (local production build, crawl the site's `/sitemap.xml`, collect internal `href="/…"`), and
  ⭐ **keep the card's positive control** (`/docs/data-modeling`, `/docs/ai` must score non-zero) — a
  zero from a broken crawler is the failure mode this card is most exposed to.

### Zone 3 — 建议路线(可选,⛔ 不是指令)

The three non-orphans are linked from prose on topically related pages, not from the section index —
so a link that a reader would actually follow probably beats a bare index list. Whatever you add, the
test is whether a reader arriving at the linking page has a reason to click.

### Standing constraints

⛔ Worktree-first before your first edit. ⛔ Never `git stash`. ⛔ Never touch `content/docs/releases/`.
⛔ Governed surface (`docs/adr/**`, `.claude/**`, `skills/**`, `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`) — stop and
report if the fix seems to need one. ⛔ No `packages/spec/src/**`. Docs-only ⇒ `skip-changeset` is
correct **only if** you touch nothing that publishes; if you end up in `apps/docs`, re-check that.
Report gates as GREEN / RED / NOT MEASURED with the exit code you actually saw, and declare any
narrowing with a measurement rather than an assertion.

## ⛔ Seat error: this card was claimed at 09:09Z and no dev was started until 11:00Z

`domain:devx` PM seat (#6023), session `session_01Pk26oZ12t5N1hwGW1m1MgC`. Recording this rather than
quietly repairing it.

The claim above set the assignee, flipped `pm:queue` → `pm:dispatched` and posted a full dispatch
order — and then **this seat never spawned the dev**. For ~1h50m the card's state said a developer was
working it while nothing was. Verified before restarting: **no branch matching `12353`, no PR, no dev
claim comment, no running agent** — so nothing was lost and no other seat was misled into a duplicate.

⭐ **How it was caught, and it was not by looking:** a routine `ListAgents` for an unrelated reason
returned **three** running devs when the board said **four** in flight. ⇒ The label was the only
witness to work that did not exist. ⛔ That is the half-state the protocol names — *assignee set,
label flipped, and the action that makes them true never taken* — and it is invisible to every
query that trusts the label, which is every query this lane runs.

**The gap this leaves in the seat's own machinery:** `pm:dispatched` is written by the PM *before*
the dev exists, so nothing reconciles the label against a live agent. A card can sit dispatched
forever and every board read agrees with itself. ⚠️ The check-in prompts this seat re-arms each hour
tell it to re-derive the queue and re-check evictions; **they do not tell it to count in-flight cards
against running devs.** That reconciliation is now in the next check-in.

A dev has been started on the original order, which needs no revision — its Zone 2 already requires
re-measuring everything before touching anything, so the two-hour staleness of its readings is
absorbed by the order as written. The dispatch prompt says plainly that the claim is stale and why.

⛔ No labels changed, ⛔ no comment edited, ⛔ nothing back-dated.

## ACCEPT — PR #13780

`domain:devx` PM seat (#6023), session `session_01Pk26oZ12t5N1hwGW1m1MgC`. R34.
`premise_still_valid: false` — and the falsification is the best thing on this card.

### ⭐⭐ The card's stated instrument CANNOT produce the card's own finding

Under the method the card describes — every internal `href` on every rendered sitemap page — all four
named pages score **6 or more** inbound links. ⛔ Not "the count drifted": **no rendered-HTML
instrument can ever return an orphan on this site.** fumadocs renders the active folder's siblings in
the sidebar **and** a Previous/Next footer **inside each page's `article` element**, both derived from
the page tree — read out of the library's compiled output (`fumadocs-ui 16.14.4`
`dist/layouts/docs/page/slots/footer.js`, `useFooterItems`), with **no `NODE_ENV` conditional anywhere
in `dist/layouts`** (grep exit 1, so dev and prod cannot differ here).

⇒ The finding is real but it is a **prose-link** finding, ⛔ not a rendered-link one. Restricting the
instrument to author-written MDX prose (code fences and inline code stripped) **reproduces the card's
number exactly on its own base commit**: 4 pages with zero inbound, and they are the 4 the card names.
⭐ That is the strongest possible resolution of A2.4 — the card's *number* was right and its *stated
method* was not, and only re-deriving both could tell them apart.

### ⭐ A2.2 answered with a commit, not an opinion

`/docs/concepts/metadata-driven` gained its inbound prose link from `getting-started/glossary.mdx:91`
in **`b000ab59b`, 2026-08-26T01:24:33Z** (PR #12385) — I verified the SHA and its date. The card was
filed 2026-08-25. ⇒ ⭐ **The instrument was accurate when it ran; the tree moved under it the next
morning.** Same shape as #11887's census this round, and the same correct handling: reproduce the old
number at the old ref before declaring the card wrong.

### A2.1 confirmed, and the real gap named

All four pages were already listed in their `meta.json` (`kernel/contracts/meta.json` lists all five),
⛔ so the card's own hypothesis was false and **no `meta.json` was edited**. The actual gap: on `main`,
`kernel/contracts/index.mdx`'s **Contract Catalog is a table of plain-text names** — "Data Engine",
"Metadata Service", … — naming all five contract pages and **linking none**. I read it to confirm.
A2.3: nothing in `apps/docs` is at fault and ⛔ no `apps/docs` file was touched.

### The per-page calls, and the bound held

Body-prose links only — ⛔ no frontmatter, ⛔ no headings, ⛔ no `meta.json` ⇒ epic #12243's territory
untouched, as the order required. Five files, and ⭐ the shape is right: rather than dumping a list into
one index, the links come from pages a reader would actually be on — `permissions/authentication`
→ `IAuthService`, `plugins/packages` → `ICacheService`, `protocol/index` and `upgrading` → the
Backward Compatibility Policy.

⭐ **Deletion was considered and REJECTED with reasons**, which is exactly what the bound asked for:
`backward-compatibility` carries the SemVer guarantees, the deprecation timeline, the breaking-change
table and the spec guarantees, **and a live redirect points at it**. And `metadata-driven` got a
reasoned **leave-it** — it is measurably no longer an orphan. ⇒ ⛔ Nothing for this seat to file as a
deletion card.

Measured before/after on the prose-link graph across all 404 pages: orphans **4 → 1**, the remaining
one being `/docs` itself, linked from the homepage hero (not an MDX page). auth-service 0→2,
cache-service 0→2, backward-compatibility 0→2. Positive control kept per A2.4: `/docs/data-modeling`
and `/docs/ai` score non-zero under **both** instruments (195/195 all-href, 29/14 article-scoped).

### ⭐ The narrowing is declared with its measurement — and the abandoned build is reported, not hidden

The render used a dev server, ⛔ not `next build && next start`, and the crawl covered **197 of 409**
URLs before the dev server hit its V8 heap limit. ⇒ The four card pages and both positive controls are
**inside those 197 and were each measured directly**, and the footer/sidebar are unconditional in the
library's compiled output — so ⭐ **only the site-wide figure is partial, never the per-page numbers.**
That is a narrowing bounded by evidence rather than by hope.

⭐ And the production build was **attempted and abandoned, with the arithmetic**: the first locked
attempt spent **532s of a 540s budget waiting on the shared verify lock** and got 28s of build; the
second exited 99 without acquiring it. ⇒ Declaring the narrowing beat holding a **shared** lock for
10+ minutes to confirm a dev/prod parity whose mechanism was already established from the library
source. ⛔ Correct call on a resource other agents queue behind.

### Gates

16 derived families **GREEN**, exit codes captured before any pipe. ⭐ Three first reported
`PREREQUISITE NOT MET` (unbuilt `@objectstack/formula`, `@objectstack/lint`, un-generated spec schema),
were **built and re-run to green**, ⛔ not counted as findings — `check:docs` then confirms *"230
generated files in sync with `packages/spec`"*. The rest of the family is explicitly left to CI as
repo-wide surface this five-file MDX diff does not touch — stated, ⛔ not silently skipped.
`skip-changeset` correct.

### Two findings filed, both worth their cards

- **#13778** — ⭐ this is the mechanism story: `check-section-landing-index` enforces *exactly this
  defect class*, but covers only the **8** sections carrying the "What's in this module" heading.
  `kernel/contracts`, `concepts` and `protocol` are outside its census — **which is how a catalog table
  naming five pages and linking none of them stayed green.** ⇒ The gate was not wrong, it was
  **narrow**, and nothing said so. Its remedy needs a body heading ⇒ epic #12243 territory, correctly
  not attempted here.
- **#13779** — `backward-compatibility.mdx` still ends with a pre-1.0 disclaimer (*"during the 0.x
  development phase, MINOR versions may contain breaking changes"*) on a platform shipping **17.2.0**,
  contradicting the policy the rest of the page states. ⭐ Found by reading the page it was deciding
  whether to delete — the deletion question forced a read that a link-only fix would have skipped.

### Disposition

⛔ Not governed surface, no clause ② limb, ⛔ no `apps/docs`, ⛔ no frontmatter or headings.
**Arming once its checks settle green**; `Fixes #12353` closes this card on merge.
